# Dataset risk assessment
I would like your help in assessing the likelihood that this data will be changed or removed from its primary location, and that users will no longer be able to access accurate and reliable copies of it, based on the rubric below.

## Sources for context
To help assess the rubric categories, perform additional research on the data, the agency, the data's topics and typical users, covering topics such as proposed regulatory or funding changes, recent news, and political commentary. This rubric is divided up into categories. Each category is divided up into risk levels. In your output, please select the appropriate risk level for each category based on your research.

### Historical Data Availability
- Gone: Data files prior to the current year or cycle are no longer publicly available.
- High Risk: Some data files prior to the current year or cycle are removed.
- Moderate Risk: Some data elements that exist in the dataset prior to the current year or cycle are removed.
- No Known Issue: Data prior to the current year or cycle remain accessible with no known alterations.

### Future Data Availability
- Gone: Data collection and publication has been terminated.
- High Risk: Statutory publication deadline missed and/or collection or publication skipped and/or ICR expired for more than one year.
- Moderate Risk: Typical or intended publication date missed and/or collection or publication delayed; ICR expired up to one year.
- No Known Issue: Data published on time or as expected and ICR active or renewed before expiration.

### Data Quality
- Gone: Data collection and publication has been terminated.
- High Risk: Reductions in granularity, timeliness, or frequency.
- Moderate Risk: Potential or emerging risk to granularity, timeliness, or frequency.
- No Known Issue: Maintained or improved granularity, timeliness, or frequency.

### Statutory Context

Monthly Wholesale Trade

About the Survey

Purpose:

  • To provide month-to-month trends for sales and inventories of U.S. merchant wholesalers, excluding manufacturers' sales branches and offices (MSBOs).
  • Title 13 of the United States Code authorizes the Census Bureau to conduct this survey and provides for voluntary responses.

Content: Companies provide estimates on monthly sales and end-of-month inventories.

Uses:

  • The Bureau of Economic Analysis uses the estimates as an input to estimate sales and inventories for the Gross Domestic Product.
  • The Council of Economic Advisers uses the estimates for assessing near term economic activity.
  • The Department of the Treasury uses the estimates to research economic trends.
  • Business and industry groups use the estimates to forecast future demand.
  • Researchers use the estimates to benchmark the results from their own sampling operations.
  • Manufacturers can use inventory estimates as a proxy for the distributors confidence for future expected sales.

Products:

  • Estimates are released 6 weeks after the close of the data month, containing preliminary current month estimates and final data for the previous month. Statistics include: sales, inventories, and inventories/sales ratios along with standard errors. Estimates are both seasonally adjusted and unadjusted.
  • An annual benchmark report is released each spring. This report presents the results of the benchmarking operation that revises monthly sales and inventories estimates based on the Annual Wholesale Trade Survey. Estimates are both seasonally adjusted and unadjusted.

Frequency: Monthly since 1936. New samples are drawn approximately every 5 years and are updated quarterly. Use of the latest sample began in April 2018.

Coverage: Companies with employment that are primarily engaged in merchant wholesale trade in the U.S, as defined by the 2012 NAICS, excluding MSBOs. Also excluded are non-merchant wholesalers such as agents, brokers, and electronic markets.

MONTHLY WHOLESALE TRADE SURVEY

PURPOSE

To track month-to-month trends for sales and inventories of U.S. distributors, jobbers, drop shippers, and import/export merchants, excluding manufacturers' sales branches or offices (MSBOs). Title 13 of the United States Code authorizes the Census Bureau to conduct this survey and provides for voluntary responses.

COVERAGE

Companies with employment that are primarily engaged in merchant wholesale trade in the U.S, as defined by the 2007 NAICS, excluding MSBOs. Also excluded are non-merchant wholesalers such as agents, brokers, and electronic markets.

CONTENT

Companies provide data on dollar values of sales and end-of-month inventories.

FREQUENCY

Monthly since 1946. New samples are drawn approximately every 5 years and are updated quarterly. Use of the latest sample began in Fall 2006.

METHODS

Data are collected by mail, fax and telephone. Response is voluntary. Questionnaires are mailed each month and request data for the month just ending.

The survey uses a stratified, one-stage design with primary strata defined by industry (e.g., Motor Vehicle and Motor Vehicle Parts, Furniture and Home Furnishings, Grocery, etc.). There are 40 primary strata. The primary strata are substratified into 4, 7, 10, or 13 annual sales size strata. The largest sales size stratum within each industry stratum consists of companies, all of which are selected with certainty (sampling weight equal to one).

The other strata are populated by EINs. Sample sizes are computed to meet multiple coefficient of variation constraints on estimated annual sales and end-of-year inventory totals. Constraints are specified at detailed industry levels and at broad industry levels up to the total wholesale level. Sampling weights range from 1 to 500. Units are selected independently between strata using simple random sampling without replacement within the size substrata. The current sample of 4,400 businesses consists of approximately 1,700 companies and 2,700 EINs. Updates to the sample are made on a quarterly basis to account for new businesses, deaths, and other changes to the universe.

PRODUCTS

Monthly Wholesale Trade Sales and Inventories reports are released 6 weeks after the close of the data month, containing preliminary current month estimates and final data for the previous month. Statistics include: sales, inventories, and inventory/sales ratios along with standard errors. Estimates are both seasonally adjusted and unadjusted.

An annual benchmark report is released each spring. This report presents the results of the benchmarking operation that revises monthly sales and inventories estimates based on the Annual Wholesale Trade Survey. Estimates are both seasonally adjusted and unadjusted.

USES

The Bureau of Economic Analysis uses the estimates as an input to estimate sales and inventories for the Gross Domestic Product.

The Council of Economic Advisers uses the estimates for assessing near term economic activity.

The Department of the Treasury uses the estimates to research economic trends.

Business and industry groups use the estimates to forecast future demand.

Researchers use the estimates to benchmark the results from their own sampling operations.

Manufacturers can use inventory estimates as a proxy for the distributors confidence for future expected sales.

SPECIAL FEATURES

Provides a designated principal economic indicator and the only source of current data on wholesale trade.

RELATED PROGRAMS

Economic Census

Annual Wholesale Trade Survey

Quarterly Financial Report

Business and Professional Classification Survey

EXPLORE INFORMATION

messages.content:
#data research
I am researching a federal dataset. Find out everything you can about this dataset, such as who publishes it, under what authority or mandate, its history, its typical users, and its benefits to the public. Be sure your research comprehensively covers each of those perspectives, as well as any others that you discover or seem useful. I believe this is accurate information, but please check:

Dataset title: Monthly Wholesale Trade
Description: The Monthly Wholesale Trade report provides national estimates of monthly sales, inventories, and inventories-to-sales ratios by kind of business for wholesale firms located in the United States (excluding manufacturers' sales branches and offices). Data from this survey provide business leaders and policymakers with an up-to-date picture of the nation's economic condition, and are a key element in estimating the quarterly Gross Domestic Product (GDP).

Return a complete report on everything that a preservationist, data librarian, data scientist, or policy activist might want to know about this data.

I checked your title and description against the Census Bureau's program pages, Federal Register notices, the monthly releases and FRED. They're accurate: the description matches the program's landing page word for word. It is a short summary, though, and leaves out several things a user needs to know (below).

# Monthly Wholesale Trade (Monthly Wholesale Trade Survey, MWTS)

## 1. Verifying what you were given

| Element | Verdict | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Title | ✅ Correct | Official program name is "Monthly Wholesale Trade"; the survey is the "Monthly Wholesale Trade Survey (MWTS)"; the release is "Monthly Wholesale Trade: Sales and Inventories." |
| Description | ✅ Matches census.gov/wholesale exactly | Missing: the survey is voluntary; it covers **merchant wholesalers only** (agents, brokers and electronic markets are excluded as well as manufacturers' sales branches and offices); figures are in current dollars with no price adjustment; it is a sample survey with sampling error. |

## 2. Publisher and governance
- **Agency:** U.S. Census Bureau (Department of Commerce), Economic Indicators Division. Data questions go to eid.wholesale.indicator.branch@census.gov; media questions go to the Public Information Office, (301) 763‑3030 / pio@census.gov.
- **Status:** Census historically calls it "a designated principal economic indicator and the only source of current data on wholesale trade." It is one of the Census Bureau's Principal Federal Economic Indicators (PFEIs), so it has fixed release times (10:00 a.m. ET) and pre-announced schedules.
- **OMB clearance:** OMB control number 0607‑0190; forms SM4217‑A and SM4217‑E. The most recent renewal ("extension without change") was published in the Federal Register on August 14, 2025.

## 3. Legal authority
- **Collection:** Title 13 U.S. Code, Sections 131 and 182.
- **Response is voluntary.** This matters because response rates directly affect data quality.
- **Confidentiality:** Title 13, Section 9 says responses can be used only for statistics and can't be published in a way that identifies a business. Transmitted data are also screened under the Federal Cybersecurity Enhancement Act of 2015.
- **Burden:** about 4,200 respondents, about 7 minutes each, about 5,880 hours a year in total, $0 in other costs.

## 4. History and timeline
- **Start date: Census's own pages disagree.** The current "About" page says "Monthly since **1936**." An older Census overview page says "Monthly since **1946**." Archivists should note this and settle it from primary sources, such as old Census publications at HathiTrust or the Federal Depository Library Program.
- Samples are redrawn every 5–7 years and updated every quarter for business births, deaths and mergers. A sample was in use from fall 2006 (about 4,400 units), and the current sample began with March 2018 data (released May 25, 2018). Existing series were restated from 2007 to 2012 industry codes (NAICS); only NAICS 4236 and 4237 changed.
- **July 28, 2016:** the first Advance Economic Indicators Report, which adds early wholesale (and retail) inventory estimates to help quarterly GDP.
- **September 19, 2022:** first experimental Monthly Wholesale Real Dollar Estimates, covering sales only.
- **September 9, 2024:** a second version added real inventories and inventories-to-sales ratios.
- **March 2025:** revisions brought in 2017 NAICS and the 2022 annual benchmark.
- **October–November 2025:** the 43‑day government shutdown delayed releases. August 2025 data came out November 21, 2025 instead of October 9. The September 2025 report came out December 11 without an Advance Economic Indicators Report. There was no October 2025 real-dollar release. Census later shortened collection windows to get back on schedule.
- **Late 2025:** Census began phasing out paper collection.
- **2026:** benchmarks now come from the **Annual Integrated Economic Survey (AIES)**, which replaced the separate Annual Wholesale Trade Survey. Revisions based on the 2023 and 2024 AIES were tentatively scheduled for **October 26, 2026**.

## 5. Content and methodology (for data scientists)
- **Universe:** U.S. employer firms primarily in merchant wholesale trade (wholesale merchants and jobbers, industrial distributors, importers and exporters). Excluded: manufacturers' sales branches and offices, NAICS 4251 (electronic markets, agents and brokers), and firms with no employees.
- **Data collected:** monthly sales, end-of-month inventories (at cost, U.S.-located goods the firm owns), number of establishments covered, and the period end date if it isn't the calendar month.
- **Sample design:** stratified, single-stage sample with 42 industry strata, each split into 4, 7, 10 or 13 sales-size groups. About 1,700 large companies are always included ("certainty" units, weight 1); about 2,500 others are chosen at random by Employer ID Number (EIN), with weights up to 500. The sampling frame is the Census Business Register.
- **Collection:** mainly by internet and email, with phone follow-up; small amounts still come by mail or fax.
- **Response rates:** in the August 2026 report, about 53.9% of sampled firms responded, covering 59.8% of sales and 61.7% of inventories by dollar value. In March 2025 the figures were 58.9%, 60.8% and 63.7%. The trend is worth watching.
- **Estimation:** weighted sums of reported and imputed data (Horvitz‑Thompson). Imputation uses similar-sized firms in the same industry. Variances use the random-groups method, and published changes come with 90% confidence intervals. An asterisk means the interval includes zero.
- **Benchmarking:** monthly levels are adjusted to annual survey totals (formerly the Annual Wholesale Trade Survey, now AIES), which are themselves tied to the Economic Census.
- **Seasonal adjustment:** X‑13ARIMA‑SEATS using X‑11 filters, adjusting for both seasonal and trading-day effects. Both adjusted and unadjusted series are published.
- **Detail:** totals, durable and nondurable goods (3-digit NAICS), and 18 four-digit NAICS kinds of business.
- **Not deflated.** Use the experimental real-dollar series (January 2012 onward, built with Bureau of Labor Statistics price indexes) for inflation-adjusted analysis.

## 6. Release cycle
Each month's data appear in three releases:
1. **Advance Economic Indicators Report:** total inventories only, about 27 days after the month ends.
2. **Monthly Wholesale Trade Report:** full sales and inventories, about 39–40 days after the month ends ("6 weeks"). It includes the prior month's revision.
3. **Manufacturing and Trade Inventories and Sales (MTIS):** about 45 days after the month ends.

There is also an annual revision report. Upcoming release dates include September 2026 data on November 9, 2026, and October 2026 data on December 9, 2026; the published schedule runs through 2027.

**Latest figures (August 2026 data, released October 8, 2026):**
- Sales: $817.5B, up 1.8% from July and up 15.6% from a year earlier.
- Inventories: $964.2B, up 0.5% from July.
- Inventories-to-sales ratio: 1.18, compared with 1.28 a year earlier.

## 7. Who uses it and why it matters
- **Bureau of Economic Analysis:** inventory and sales inputs to GDP, including the inventory valuation adjustment.
- **Bureau of Labor Statistics:** Producer Price Indexes and productivity measures.
- **Council of Economic Advisers:** assessing near-term economic activity.
- **Treasury:** research on economic trends.
- **Federal Reserve and markets:** inventory cycles and recession signals; the inventories-to-sales ratio is closely watched.
- **Businesses and trade groups:** forecasting demand. Manufacturers read distributor inventories as a sign of distributors' confidence in future sales.
- **Researchers:** checking their own samples against it.

The public benefit is free, timely, statistically documented information on the economy's distribution and supply-chain layer, which no private source covers comprehensively.

## 8. Access points (for data librarians and preservationists)
- Program home: census.gov/wholesale. It has the current report (HTML, PDF and Excel), historical reports, annual revisions, real-dollar tables, definitions, FAQs and methodology PDFs.
- Archived PDFs follow the pattern www2.census.gov/wholesale/pdf/mwts/historic/mwts_YYYYMM.pdf.
- Time series tool: census.gov/econ/currentdata/?programCode=MWTS.
- Census API: the economic indicators time series. Census says the URL now includes /timeseries/; I believe the path is /data/timeseries/eits/mwts, but check it on the Census developers page.
- FRED (release 290) mirrors the data from January 1992, for example S42SMNM144NCEN (sales, not seasonally adjusted) and I42IMSM144SCEN (inventories, seasonally adjusted). FRED's AMINVTS series holds the advance inventory estimates.

**Preservation notes:**
- Monthly releases overwrite earlier figures, and annual benchmarks rewrite history. Keeping each release as published is the only way to study revisions.
- Several "About" pages are out of date: they still say 2012 NAICS and "latest sample April 2018" despite the 2017 NAICS change and the move to AIES. I couldn't confirm whether a newer sample has been introduced.
- Older series were built on earlier industry codes (SIC before NAICS). Check comparability before splicing long series together.
- Census asks anyone who builds new estimates from these figures to cite Census only for the original estimates.

## 9. Issues for policy advocates
- **Voluntary response and falling response rates** reduce precision and increase reliance on imputation.
- **Vulnerability to funding lapses:** the 2025 shutdown showed how a gap in appropriations disrupts a Principal Federal Economic Indicator.
- **Coverage gaps:** wholesale activity by manufacturers' sales branches and by brokers isn't in the monthly survey, and the survey is national only, with no state data.
- **Public comment:** OMB renewals in the Federal Register are formal chances to comment on usefulness, burden and quality.
